resources.string: Not installed · Review a design before any code

Google\'s Elephant-Goldfish Model (open source, Apache 2.0). The agent (the Elephant) works out a design with you and writes it down. Then fresh reviewers (the Goldfish), who never saw your conversation, read only the document and try to break it. The design is fixed until it passes and you approve it; only then is code written.
It uses more tokens than a plain chat: every reviewer reads the document, its persona and project files. On a phone, Quick or Standard reviewers are usually enough.
Deletes EGM and its rules files from the phone. Design documents and reports in your projects stay.
Type one at the start of a message in any chat; the rest of the message is the task.
On: you see every stage\'s report before the next stage runs. Off: all stages run, then one combined report.
How often a review stage may run again once the document is fixed. 0 = never.
Each running reviewer is a full agent: more at once is faster but needs more memory.
The /egm commands stop working. Your design documents and reports stay in your projects.
A little buddy that floats over the app. Drag it around or fling it, tap or double-tap it, long-press it for its menu. It thinks while your agent works and cheers when it\'s done.
It will float on your screens
You can change this anytime in Settings → Appearance.
Which command to use when, with examples, and what happens in a normal chat and in a Jarvis chat.
For a new feature or a big change, where a wrong design costs a lot: several files, data formats, APIs. Uses the most tokens.

1. The agent asks you questions until the idea is clear (brainstorm). 2. It writes the design document, section by section, and asks for your OK on each. 3. The reviewers attack the document; the agent fixes it or explains why a finding is wrong. 4. You approve the design. 5. Only then does it write the code.
/egm add offline sync for notes, with conflict handling
For small changes: a bug fix, a refactor, a small feature, a change to a spec. Much cheaper than /egm.

1. The agent first points out risks and gaps in the task, then waits. 2. Type checklist: it writes a short plan (egm_lite_checklist.md). 3. Type goldfish: one fresh reviewer checks the plan (you can skip this). 4. Type exec: it makes the change. 5. Type review: one fresh reviewer checks the changes.
/egm-lite fix the crash when the chat list is empty
When a plan or design document already exists (yours, or written in another chat) and you want it checked before anyone builds it.
The reviewers check the document and the agent writes their findings into a report. Then you choose: the agent fixes the findings, you fix them yourself, or you stop there.

Normal chat (Claude Code, Codex, …): the agent does everything in that chat and runs the reviewers as its own hidden sub-agents. The simplest and lightest way. If the agent has no sub-agent tool, it stops and tells you to use a Jarvis chat.

Jarvis chat (Jarvis tab → a Jarvis chat, then type the command): Jarvis manages the run. It starts a planner chat (or plans itself, see Jarvis below) and one chat per reviewer, which you can open from the chat list. The phases show as Jarvis\' mission steps, and Jarvis asks you to approve the design. Use it to watch the reviewers, or when the agent has no sub-agent tool. Every reviewer chat is a full agent, so it needs more memory.

• Answer the agent\'s questions: it asks one at a time. • Everything is saved as files in your project, in %1$s/<topic>/: the design document and every review report. Open them in Files. • Nothing is coded before you approve. To approve, just say so; or ask for changes, or for one more review round. • You can stop at any time. The files stay, and later you can check the document again with /egm-review.

• Start with Quick or Standard reviewers; Full runs eight reviewers in every round. • If the phone gets slow, set Reviewers at the same time to 1. • Write the task as you would explain it to a colleague: what, why, and any limits ("no new libraries"). • For a change of a few lines, a plain chat is cheaper than EGM.
EGM\'s published release, checked against its checksum. The stable choice.
EGM\'s main branch as it is now, with skills not released yet (egm-lite, as of release 0.1.1). It changes almost daily and has no checksum to check it against.
EGM: brainstorm → design doc → Goldfish review → your approval → code
EGM lite: checklist → one Goldfish review → code → diff review
EGM: Goldfish review of an existing design document
Skeptical architect: a simpler design, no extras, reuse of existing code
Looks for a different approach that removes the core trade-off
Naive reader: explains the design back, flags undefined terms and gaps
Hostile critic: architecture, failure cases, scaling and cost
The document\'s layout: sections, headings, missing parts
Copy editor: clear, precise, no filler
Tech lead: can the plan be built step by step without guessing
Checks the plan against the real code: files, APIs, names
Jarvis starts a planner chat that brainstorms, writes and fixes the design; Jarvis relays and runs the reviewers. Keeps Jarvis\' own chat light.
Jarvis brainstorms and writes the design in its own chat and runs the reviewers. One chat less, but Jarvis\' context fills up.
Which of EGM\'s reviewer personas look at a design (/egm and /egm-review). Each is a separate reviewer run that costs tokens. /egm-lite always uses one reviewer.
Who is the Elephant (writes and fixes the design) when you type an EGM command in a Jarvis chat. The reviewers are always separate chats that Jarvis starts.
Not available: EGM %1$s has no egm-lite. Install the development version (step 1) to get it now; a later EGM release will include it too.

Downloads EGM from GitHub (the skills, the reviewer personas and the review standards) into a folder every agent on this phone can read. Pick where it comes from:

In a normal chat the agent runs the reviewers with its own subagent tool. In a Jarvis chat (Jarvis tab), Jarvis manages the run: it starts every reviewer as a separate chat, shows the phases as its mission steps and asks you to approve the design.
